confirmed.description: The hall set changes between panels on the same page. In 2.1 and 2.2 the courtiers sit cross-legged on floor mats, the floor is matted, and Varma sits cross-legged at his map on a low wooden platform. In 2.5 the courtiers sit in rows on wooden benches or chairs, the floor is polished stone, and Varma sits in a throne chair on a high stepped stone dais against a red backdrop. The script asks for 'a slightly raised wooden platform' with the map on the mat, and later hall panels (6.1, 6.3, 9.5) go back to courtiers seated on the floor, so 2.5 is the odd one out.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of 2.5 bottom-left: bare-chested courtiers seated on wooden bench backs/armrests along a shiny tiled floor; 2.5 right: five-step stone dais, Varma in a gilt chair. Compare 2.1 (men cross-legged on mats, matted floor) and 2.2 (Varma cross-legged on a cushion on a wooden platform, map on the mat).

verdict.reason: Confirmed on crops of 2.5 compared with 2.1, 2.2 and 2.3. In 2.5 the courtiers on both sides sit at bench or chair height, and wooden armrests or seat ends show below their elbows at bottom left and bottom right. The floor is polished stone with reflections. Varma sits in a high-backed chair against a red backdrop, on a stone dais with three to four steps, and has no map. On the same page, 2.1 shows men sitting cross-legged on a matted floor, and 2.2 and 2.3 both show Varma cross-legged on a low wooden platform with the map on the mat in front of him. The script says "men sit cross-legged in loose rows" and "a slightly raised wooden platform", and 2.5 is meant to show those same seated rows from the entrance end. So 2.5 contradicts the script and the three panels above it. One correction to the original report: the throne and stepped dais are not unique to 2.5. 6.1, 6.4 and 9.5 also put Varma in a carved throne on a stepped dais, so the throne versus floor-platform question is split across the whole chapter, and there 2.2 and 2.3 are the odd ones. What only 2.5 gets wrong is the courtiers on benches or chairs. Every other hall panel (2.1, 2.3, 6.1, 6.3, 9.5) seats them on the floor, and benches are also implausible for a Travancore audience hall of the 1740s. The panel is full width, so the change is clearly visible at print size, but it is limited to one panel's set. Severity is major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: Varma's seat is a prop that changes across the chapter, and the lettering contradicts the art. In 2.2 he is drawn seated on the mat. From 2.5 and 3.3 onward he sits in a gilt throne chair with red cushions and lion-head arms (3.3, 3.4, 5.5, 6.1, 6.2, 6.4, 8.5, 9.5, 10.2). Ramayyan's line in 10.2 refers to the king's mat, and the 8.5 beat has him tap the spear 'against the mat', yet both panels show him on a throne.
confirmed.evidence: 10.2: a gold lion-head armrest is visible beside Varma's hip, under the balloon 'He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat.' 8.5: Varma sits on a throne flanked by carved lion heads, with the spear butt tapping the floor. 2.2: he sits cross-legged on a cushion at floor level with the map spread on the mat.

verdict.reason:
The seat drift is real, so I can't refute it. It is weaker than reported, and 10.2 is a poor place to anchor it.

What the art shows: In 2.1 and 2.2 Varma sits cross-legged at floor level on the platform, with the map on the mat. From 2.5 on he sits in a raised chair with red cushions and lion-head arms (3.3, 3.4, 8.5). This throne also clashes with the novel and the script. Both put him on a mat on a slightly raised wooden platform (novel line 37: "a rolled map on the mat before him"). Ramayyan's 10.2 line, "too many lives to sit on that mat", depends on that humble mat image, and a gilt lion throne blunts it.

Why it is minor, not major:
(1) In 10.2 the throne shows only as one small gold lion-head ornament by Varma's hip, partly blocked by the lower balloon. At print size nothing in the panel visibly contradicts the line, and "that mat" still reads as a figure for his royal seat.
(2) The 8.5 crop shows a woven mat under the throne, and the spear butt with its tap ticks lands on it. So the script beat "taps the butt of his spear against the mat" is literally met.
(3) The switch from 2.2 to 2.5 has an easy in-story reading: the king was studying the map at floor level, then took his seat for the audience. In 3.1 the map is moved to a low stand in front of the seat, which supports that reading.

What remains is prop drift across the chapter, not a localized error on page 10. If the author wants the novel's mat image kept, the fix is to the throne panels (2.5 onward) or a note in the bible. 10.2 does not need redrawing on its own account.

confirmed.description: The hall plan is flipped. Varma faces the camera from the platform, so the open sea side (his right hand) should be on screen left, as the fixed hall plan requires and as 4.1 on the same page shows. In 4.5 the open side, with palms, beach and sea, is behind him on screen RIGHT. In 4.4 the sea also sits on screen left behind the seated Nagoji, while 4.3, a moment earlier from the same angle, correctly puts the open side on screen right.
confirmed.evidence: 4.5 crop: bright window onto palms and the coastline at the right edge, behind the [in Malayalam] balloon; the closed wooden wall and a carved chair are at screen left. 4.1: open pillars and a parapet on screen left behind Varma. 4.4: open sea between the pillars on screen left behind Nagoji. 4.3: tiled eave and palm on screen right.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed for 4.5 only. The 4.4 part is refuted.

**4.5 (flipped):** Varma faces the camera, leaning over the map. Behind him the closed carved wooden wall and chair are on screen left. A bright opening onto palms, beach, coastline and sea is on screen RIGHT, which is his left hand. The hall plan says the open sea side is on the king's right hand, so with Varma facing camera it belongs on screen left. Both the script note and the chapter notes say this plan is fixed for every hall panel.

Every other shot toward the platform keeps the plan:
- 4.1, on the same page: Varma faces camera with open pillars, palms and parapet on screen left, and the plain wall on screen right.
- Page 3, panels 3.1 and 3.3: the open side, with palms and the fort, is on screen left.

So 4.5 is the one panel that flips it. The sea window is big, bright and easy to spot at print size. It also sits directly under 4.1, so the same king on the same page has the sea on opposite sides. The script's 4.5 text leaves out the hall-plan tag, which probably let the generator flip it, but the fixed plan in the notes still applies.

The fix is a background flip (open sea side to screen left, closed wall to screen right). Varma's figure and the lettering can stay. That makes it a localized major issue, not a blocker.

**4.4 (not flipped):** Nagoji faces three-quarters toward screen right, and Varma's cloth shows at the right foreground edge. That puts the platform at screen right, so this is a side view from the closed wall looking out. In that view the open side falls behind the seated figure, as drawn, with sea between the pillars. It is the mirror of the 3.4 side view and fits the plan. 4.3 is correct, with the open side on screen right, as the reviewer said.

confirmed.description: The page doesn't read as a coherent comic page. All five panels are stacked in one column at five different widths, each centred, with no shared outer frame, so both edges of the page are ragged and there are large cream margins. 8.3 is less than half the frame width. This is unlike the approved Chapter 1 grid.
confirmed.evidence: Panel scan, page 8, in x extents: 8.1 runs 330 to 1508, 8.2 runs 241 to 1597, 8.3 runs 516 to 1321, 8.4 runs 268 to 1569, and 8.5 runs 205 to 1633. The frame used on every other page is 148 to 1689.

verdict.reason:
The measurements are right, but the problem is minor, not major. I measured the page 8 render (1838 px wide) and got the same figures as the reviewer: 8.1 runs 330 to 1507, 8.2 runs 241 to 1596, 8.3 runs 516 to 1320, 8.4 runs 268 to 1568 and 8.5 runs 205 to 1632. The column is 148 to 1688. It is the s3 fitted layout, five single rows of [84.6, 192.8, 61.9, 93.7, 82.5] pt.

Two parts of the claim do not hold:
1. "Unlike the approved Chapter 1 grid" is wrong. Chapter 1 r6 uses the same centred rows of varying width. Ch01 page 6 has three inset rows stacked in a row (207 to 1630, 414 to 1422, 261 to 1575), and its narrow middle row is an eyes close-up strip that 8.3 visibly echoes. Ch01 pages 2, 3, 4, 5, 7 and 8 also have inset rows, and so do ch06 pages 3, 4 and 7. This is house style.
2. 8.3 being narrow is scripted ("Narrow, cold"). The page reads in a single unambiguous column with even gutters, so "doesn't read as a coherent comic page" is overstated.

What remains is real but small:
- Page 8 is the only page in ch06 or ch01 with no row reaching the column edges. Every other page has at least one full-span row holding the frame.
- The script marks 8.2 ("Large, full width") and 8.5 ("Full width, bottom") as full width. They span only 88 percent and 93 percent of the column, below the pipeline's own 95 percent rule for full-width panels (pipeline/README.md).
- At print size that is about 0.3 in of cream on each side of 8.2 and 0.6 in beside 8.1, so the edges look ragged.

The fix is a layout refit, not a redraw: give 8.2 and 8.5 the full 95 percent column span, or regroup 8.3 and 8.4, as the s1 and s2 layouts did. It is polish, not major.

confirmed.description: Awkward crop. The top border cuts off Varma's cream-and-gold turban and its jewelled peacock-feather crest (the chapter's visual lock for him), leaving only the lower band. The 'Ram.' balloon is jammed against the same top edge.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of 8.5: Varma's head is cut at the turban's lower band, about 10 to 25px from the top border, and no crest or feather is visible. Every other Varma panel in the chapter shows the crest.

verdict.reason: The crop is real, but it should be minor, not major. On page 8, panel 8.5 (zoomed crop around x 680-880, y 2185-2300 of the 1838x2775 render), the panel's top border cuts across Varma's forehead at the tilak line. Only the lower cream-and-gold band of the turban shows, and no jewelled peacock-feather crest appears. The script (8.5) asks for a 'cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest', and CONTINUITY.md line 52 gives that look for formal court audiences, so the crest is required here, not optional. Why minor: the costume itself is right (the turban is there, just framed out), his identity is clear (face from the sheet, pearl earrings, gold necklaces, cream-and-gold cloth, spear), and the action is not hidden. The spear butt on the mat with the motion ticks, the bird on the parapet, the sea on screen left and the 'Ram.' line are all present and readable. The second half of the claim does not hold. The 'Ram.' balloon sits fully inside the frame, has clear margins, reads cleanly and points correctly at Varma, so it is not a lettering defect. The fix is a polish reframe: drop the figure, or add headroom so the crest clears the top border. Nothing needs to be redrawn.

confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tail. The tail on Ramayyan's 'Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders...' points to Varma's knee and lap, so the king appears to say it. That breaks the Malayalam-only convention and makes 'show him' illogical. Ramayyan is seated to the right and only the second balloon points to him.
confirmed.evidence: Zoomed crop of 9.5: the left balloon's tail ends on the gold-bordered drape over Varma's knee, directly below Varma. Ramayyan's head is about 150px to the right.

verdict.reason: I confirm this is a real problem. It is major, not a blocker. I zoomed in on panel 9.5 (crop of page-09.png, original pixels about 901-1692 x 1900-2538). The tail of the left balloon ("Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders...") climbs up and to the right and stops on the gold-bordered end of Varma's shawl, where it hangs over his right knee and the arm of his throne. Varma is the large figure sitting directly above that balloon. Ramayyan's robe begins about 50px to the right of the tail tip at 300 DPI, and his head is about 190px away. If you extend the tail's line, it would reach Ramayyan's lap, but readers judge the speaker by where the tip lands, and the tip lands on the king. Only the second balloon ("If you are wrong...") clearly points to Ramayyan. The script's lettering note for the whole chapter (CHAPTER-06-SCRIPT.md, line 73, restated in the notes at line 364) says Varma's only lettered word in Chapter 6 is "Ram." Every other line from him is a bare "[in Malayalam]" tag that Ramayyan translates. So a full English sentence that looks like it comes from Varma breaks a convention the script sets for the whole chapter. It also makes "show him" read oddly, since "him" means the king. Nothing in the bible or the script allows this. The two balloons sit side by side, so some readers will work out that one man speaks both lines, which keeps it from being a blocker. The fix is small: move the tail tip about 60-150px right so it reaches Ramayyan's robe or hand, or link the two balloons with a connector. That makes it a localized speaker-tail error, which the rubric rates as major.

confirmed.description: Ramayyan's long line 'Outside this fort a strip of shore runs along the sea...' has no tail, even though he is off panel. Set next to Varma's tag in a panel showing only Varma, it reads as Varma's speech. It is also a 12-line column of two or three words per line, and it covers the right third of the view: the sea and the strip of wet sand that the script says must clearly plant the Chapter 7 ground.
confirmed.evidence: Zoomed crop: the balloon is a closed tall oval with no tail, running from the top area down to the bottom border. Behind it, only the left edge of the beach and the bluff show. The sea strip is hidden.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed on page 9, panel 9.4. Checked with a full-resolution crop of the r2 render and compared against the raw frame (chapters/ch06/frames/page-09-panel-04-v01.png).

1. **No tail on the speech balloon.** Ramayyan's balloon is a closed, tall oval and has no tail at all. Varma is the only figure in the panel. His "[in Malayalam]" balloon sits right next to it with a tail pointing to his mouth, so the long English balloon reads as Varma continuing to speak. This chapter already has a rule for off-panel speakers: on page 5, panel 5.4, "You mistrust pilots?" has a tail pointing to the panel edge. Panel 9.4 breaks that rule. It also undercuts the script's device that Varma's Malayalam is never translated in his own balloons.

2. **The balloon hides the sea.** It is lettered as a narrow column of 12 lines and fills about the right 40% of the panel, from near the top border down to the bottom border. The raw frame has open sea with surf, the strip of wet sand and the fort on the bluff in that area. In the render, the balloon covers almost all of the sea; only a thin sliver of surf shows beside the sand and at the far right edge. The bluff, the palms and part of the sand are still visible. But the script asks for the strip "pinned between" the bluff and the sea, and says "plant it clearly". The sea half of that is lost.

**Fix:** re-letter only, no redraw needed. Give the balloon a tail pointing to the panel edge, re-flow the text wider and shorter, and move it into the sky area at the top right. The ground shown here is set up for Chapter 7, so this is more than polish, but it is a local lettering fix. Severity: major, not blocker.

confirmed.description: Varma's seat doesn't match the script. In 2.2 he sits cross-legged on a mat on a slightly raised wooden platform, as written. From 3.3 on he sits on a tall carved throne chair, and in 6.1 and 9.5 that throne is at the top of a stepped dais. The script ties the king to the mat: 8.5 has him tap his spear 'against the mat', and the 10.2 lettering says 'He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat'. The throne art contradicts those lines and the humble working hall of 'They did not take me to a palace'.
confirmed.evidence: 3.4, left third: Varma sits in a carved wooden throne with a red seat and a round gold-rimmed bolster, feet on a footstool. 6.1: the throne sits at the top of a dais of about three steps, high above Nagoji's mat. 10.2: a gold lion-head throne armrest shows beside Varma's knee, directly under the balloon 'He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat.' 9.5: Varma and Ramayyan both sit in carved chairs at the top of steps.

verdict.reason:
Confirmed. The art shows the problem, and nothing in the script or the bible allows it.

**What the source says.** The script for 2.2 asks for "a slightly raised wooden platform" with "a rolled map … open on the mat before him". The novel's chapter 6 says the same: "on a slightly raised wooden platform … the mat before him". The novel also has the spear-tap "against the mat", and its line "He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat" means the king's own seat. The bible's Marthanda Varma line (CONTINUITY.md line 52) covers dress only. It says nothing about a throne or a dais.

**What the renders show.**
- **2.1 and 2.2:** Varma sits cross-legged on a mat on a low platform, as written.
- **2.5:** a stepped dais with a seated figure already appears at the far end.
- **3.3:** a red-cushioned throne arm and a round gold-rimmed bolster sit beside him.
- **3.4 (crop):** a carved wooden throne with a red seat and the gold-rimmed bolster, his feet on a footstool. He sits high above Ramayyan's floor table.
- **6.1 (crop):** a full throne chair on top of a dais of about three dark stone steps, high above Nagoji's mat. Ramayyan is also on a chair on the dais.
- **6.2 and 6.4:** a lion-head throne arm, and a chair on a dais.
- **8.5 (crop):** a lion-arm throne with red bolsters. There is a woven mat under it, so the spear-tap beat on the mat still technically reads.
- **9.5:** Varma and Ramayyan both sit in carved chairs at the top of steps.
- **10.2 (crop):** a small gold lion-head armrest shows by Varma's knee, right under the balloon "He has spent too many lives to sit on that mat."

**Why this is not too slight to matter.** It is a continuity break inside the chapter: he sits on a mat in 2.2, then on a dais throne from 3.3 on. It is plainly visible at print size in 3.4, 6.1, 8.5 and 9.5. It undercuts the chapter's point: "They did not take me to a palace", and the contrast with the Deccan kings' grand halls.

**Severity: major, not blocker.** Identity, costume, lettering and story beats are all intact, and the 8.5 spear-tap still lands on a mat under the throne. The 10.2 lion head is small; it is the 3.4, 6.1 and 9.5 thrones that carry the error. It is a staging and set error repeated across about seven panels. The fix is to redraw Varma's seat as a mat on a low wooden platform, with no chair and no stepped dais.

confirmed.description: Wrong speaker tail. 'Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders...' is Ramayyan's line, but its tail points at Varma. This reads as the king speaking Konkani, which breaks the chapter's rule that Varma's only lettered word is 'Ram.' Secondary: the panel should be a high shot from the entrance end with Nagoji small below the platform. It is drawn as a low side view with Nagoji kneeling at the left edge.
confirmed.evidence: The large lower-centre balloon's tail runs up and right and ends on Varma's knee and the arm of his throne (around x=1220, y=2270 in the original). The next balloon, 'If you are wrong...', correctly points to Ramayyan.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from crops of page-09.png at full resolution (1838x2775). Panel 9.5 has a wrong speaker tail. The tail of the "Take the Madurai horse and a hundred Maravar riders..." balloon ends at about x=1232, y=2277. That point is on the gold-fringed end of Varma's shawl, where it hangs over his right knee beside the throne. Ramayyan's body starts at about x=1285, so the tip touches only Varma. The script gives the line to RAMAYYAN. The page 3 lettering note says Varma's only lettered words in the chapter are "Ram.", and everything else he says is set as "[in Malayalam]". As drawn, the king seems to speak a full Konkani line, which breaks that rule. The wording ("show him") hints that Ramayyan is the speaker, but the tail still reads as Varma's. The next balloon, "If you are wrong...", points correctly up to Ramayyan's lap and scroll. This is a localized lettering fix: move the tail tip about 80 to 150 px right and up, onto Ramayyan. That makes it major, not blocker; the line itself is correct and readable. The staging point is also real but minor on its own. The script asks for a high shot from the entrance end with Nagoji small below the platform. The render is a near eye-level three-quarter side view with Nagoji kneeling at the left. The beat still reads: Nagoji on the mat, the king and the diwan on the platform above him.

confirmed.description: The script calls this the place to 'plant clearly' the Chapter 7 ground: a narrow strip of wet sand pinned between a laterite bluff with palms and the sea, filling the right two thirds. A tall Ramayyan balloon covers the right half of the view. The sea is almost entirely hidden, so the strip doesn't read as 'pinned between' bluff and sea. Varma also takes up about 40 percent of the width rather than the near left third.
confirmed.evidence: In the right panel of row 2, the balloon 'Outside this fort a strip of shore runs along the sea...' runs the full panel height on the right side. Only the bluff and a wedge of beach show between the pillar and the balloon. Water shows only as a sliver at the far lower-right corner.

verdict.reason: The problem is real but smaller than reported, so I'm calling it minor rather than major. On page 9, panel 9.4, the Ramayyan balloon ("Outside this fort a strip of shore runs along the sea...") is a tall, narrow one-column balloon. It covers about the right 30 to 35 percent of the panel from top to bottom. The open sea sits under it. Water shows only as a wet sheen and a foam line at the edge of the beach, between the pillar and the balloon, plus a sliver at the lower-right corner. So the "pinned between bluff and sea" idea the script asks to "plant clearly" reads weakly. Still, the Chapter 7 ground is clearly there between the pillars: a red laterite bluff topped with coconut palms, a fort wall, a narrow rock-strewn sand beach at its foot, and the waterline. The dialogue in the same panel names the sea, so the beat is not missing. The reviewer also overstates Varma's size. He takes up about 34 percent of the panel width (0 to 260 px of a 775 px crop), which is in line with the "near left third" direction. The art probably doesn't need a redraw. The fix is to reletter: use a wider, shorter balloon, or split it in two, over the sky in the upper right, so the sea shows below it.

confirmed.description: The hearsay stain is meant to hold a padre followed by a column of Portuguese musketeers, with Nagoji small at the lower edge and Varma's hand tapping the spear shaft at the foreground edge. The balloons hide the musketeer column, and Varma's hand tap doesn't show at all. Nagoji is drawn large in the left foreground, so the panel reads as a portrait of Nagoji talking rather than a memory image.
confirmed.evidence: Behind the padre, only one partial soldier (a hat brim, a buff sleeve and a matchlock) shows before the 'Our clerks said...' balloon. The right edge shows only a strip of gold-bordered cloth and a dark shaft, with no hand. Nagoji, cross-legged, fills about the left third of the panel at full height.

verdict.reason: Confirmed on page 4, panel 4.4. The cause is the lettering, not the drawing. The selected frame (chapters/ch06/frames/page-04-panel-04-v02.png) does contain everything the script asks for: a full column of about ten musketeers in broad plumed hats and buff coats with matchlocks behind the padre, and Varma's hand gripping the spear shaft at the right foreground edge. In the r2 render both are hidden. The 'Our clerks said...' balloon covers the whole column, leaving only the first soldier's hat brim, a buff sleeve and a matchlock. The 'We heard of rajas...' balloon covers Varma's hand. One correction to the reviewer: the right edge strip shows more than cloth and a shaft. A sliver of his forearm with the gold bead bracelet also shows between the two balloons, but the hand and the tap gesture cannot be seen, so the beat does not read. That leaves half of the stain's two subjects missing: the soldiers that 'the men behind count how many guns' refers to. The king's small reaction beat is lost too. The composition point also holds. In both the raw frame and the render, Nagoji sits large in the left foreground, about a third of the panel wide and at full height, not 'small at the lower edge'. The panel therefore reads as Nagoji talking with a padre behind him, not as a hearsay image. Severity is major, not blocker. The problem is localized, and most of it can be fixed by re-lettering: smaller or reflowed balloons placed over the empty smoke above and left of the padre, or over the floor at bottom centre, would uncover the column and the hand without a redraw. Nagoji's size alone is a composition deviation that does not break the beat.

refuted.description: Ramayyan's face is mostly hidden in his solo medium shot. Two balloons cover his crown, so the receding hairline that identifies him does not show. The left balloon also covers the left half of his face, leaving one eye, the nose and the mouth. His bare forearms are drawn thick and muscular, not the thin frame of the sheet and the bible.
refuted.reason: Refuted after zooming in on 9.1. The claim that the left balloon covers the left half of his face is wrong. That balloon only covers the back of his head and part of the ear. Both eyes show, though the tail of the upper balloon clips the outer corner of the far eye. The heavy brows, the mole on the near cheek, the thin nose and mouth, and the lined forehead all show, and they match his face in 9.3 and on the sheet (03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15.png). One part of the claim is true: the "Our Maravar riders..." balloon sits over his crown, so the receding hairline is hidden. But that is balloon placement, not a drawing error; it doesn't contradict the bible's "receding hair". His identity is never in doubt. He is the only figure in the panel, and the script puts the king out of frame. The white cloth, stylus, palm-leaf bundles and low table follow the bible and the script. The bald crown also reads clearly on the same page in 9.2, 9.3 and 9.5. The forearms are sinewy with some vein detail, not bulky or muscular. That is within normal variation for a thin man and too slight to matter at print size. At most, moving the top balloon slightly up or right would be optional lettering polish. It doesn't call for a redraw or a major flag.

minors.description: Nagoji's ear ornament is a hanging gold drop, not the small flush gold stud set by the bible and the author's decision of 2026-10-02. At 10.5 it changes again, to a small crescent or hoop. Per that decision, ch1-8 panels with a drop are a known deviation to list for the author, not to redraw automatically.
minors.evidence: 10.1: long teardrop pendants hang on short links from both ears. 5.2: drops in both ears. 5.1, 5.4, 4.3 and 6.3: a ball drop hangs below the lobe. 10.5: the ear in profile shows a C-shaped gold hoop. 8.4 is the closest to a stud (a ball on a post).

minors.description: In this profile close-up, Nagoji's chin and jaw show visible stubble. The bible requires a clean-shaven chin and allows light stubble only in captivity. In ch6 he is in his post-captivity village look.
minors.evidence: Page 8, panel 4: his face in left profile at the upper right. Stippled dark stubble runs along the jawline and under the lower lip to the chin. A fainter version appears on the chin at 5.1 (eyes closed, head tipped back). Elsewhere, for example 8.1, 10.1 and 10.3, the chin is clean.

minors.description: This is Ramayyan's introduction panel (the caption names him), but the top panel border cuts his head at the eyebrows. His most distinctive feature from the sheet and the bible, the receding hairline and bald crown, does not show. The script's production note says this 2.4 frame becomes his reference for later panels, so the missing hairline will carry forward.
minors.evidence: Page 2, panel 4: the frame edge runs just above his brows. Only black curls at both temples are visible, which on their own read as a full head of hair. By contrast, in 2.2, 3.3 and 6.2 the high bald forehead is clear.

minors.description: Ramayyan's seat is inconsistent on the same page. In 9.1 he sits on the floor mat at his low table. In 9.5 he sits in a red-and-gold throne-style chair on the dais, level with the king. The same gilt chair appears in 6.1, 6.4 and 10.2. The script and 2.4 place him at a low table beside the platform, and the matching throne weakens the king and diwan hierarchy.
minors.evidence: 9.1: cross-legged behind a low wooden table on a woven mat. 9.5: seated in a carved chair with red upholstery and gold finials beside Varma's throne on the stepped dais.

minors.description: Two elements of the stain are missing or barely there. The 'column of Portuguese musketeers in broad tilted hats and buff leather coats' is a single half-hidden figure in the smoke behind the padre. The foreground beat of Varma's hand tapping the spear shaft is absent: there is only a strip of cream-and-gold cloth at the right edge and no hand or shaft.
minors.evidence: 4.4 crop: one figure with a hat brim and a matchlock, partly hidden behind the padre's shoulder; the right edge shows the cloth edge and a wooden post, with no hand on a shaft.

minors.description: Prop mismatch in the inset. Ramayyan's writing tool is drawn as a gold-barrelled pen with a metal nib, writing on a thick wooden board. Everywhere else (2.4, 5.3, 5.5, 9.1) he uses a thin stylus on palm-leaf bundles, and the script asks for a 'stylus, scratching fast on a palm leaf'.
minors.evidence: 4.5 inset, top left: a brass pen with a tapered nib, held to a plank-like wooden surface; no palm leaf is visible.

minors.description: The background is inconsistent with the rest of the hall scene. The guards in this panel wear maroon-red turbans and white tunics, while every other hall guard on this page and elsewhere (6.1, 6.3, 4.2, 5.1) is bare-headed with a topknot. The view through the open side shows a sandstone castle with towers on a hill and a large multi-masted European ship. In 7.3 and 7.5 the same open side looks onto the small inlet, local boats and the red laterite wall.
minors.evidence: 6.4 zoom: three guards in red turbans with red waist sashes behind Ibrahim; a European-looking hilltop fortress and a white three-masted ship are visible between the pillars.

minors.description: Setting inconsistency at the gate. Behind it stands a whitewashed two-storey European colonial-style mansion with an arcaded facade and a tiled tower. It reads as Portuguese Goa rather than the Travancore fort just established in 1.3, which shows an open timber hall on a laterite wall and no such building.
minors.evidence: 1.4 crop: a white building with rows of arched windows, a red tiled roof and a small tower, centred between Nagoji's head and Ibrahim's turban.

minors.description: Staging continuity. Nagoji appears seated or crouched among the courtiers, with his bandaged forearms resting low across his knees and Ibrahim stooping to his ear. Yet 2.1 shows him just entering, and 2.5 shows him walking down the lane into the clear space. He has not reached the mat yet.
minors.evidence: 2.3 bottom: Nagoji's horizontal bandaged forearms and white dhoti at knee height in the foreground, Ibrahim bent low over him, the seated rows level with them behind.

minors.description: The panel's top edge crops Varma's turban above the forehead, so the jewelled peacock-feather crest, a costume lock for every panel of this audience, is out of frame. It is his last full-figure appearance on the page.
minors.evidence: 8.5 zoom: only the lower band of the cream-and-gold turban shows at the frame edge, with no feather or jewel visible; all other Varma panels show the crest.

minors.description: This is Ramayyan's introductory close, which the production notes say becomes his reference frame. The top crop hides his signature receding hairline and bald crown, leaving what reads as a full head of curly hair. That weakens it as a reference.
minors.evidence: 2.4 zoom: his curls run to the panel border directly above the forehead; the bald crown on the approved sheet (03-ramayyan-dalawa-v15.png) is not visible.

minors.description: The art contradicts the line it illustrates. Nagoji says the bastions are built 'thick and low, so cannonballs skip off', but the stain shows a tall, steep, crenellated fortress wall on a rocky crag with cannons on top. Also, the bandaged hand 'shaping a low wall in the air' is out of frame.
minors.evidence: 4.3 left: a multi-tier stone wall rising high above the surf, with the ball striking near its top; Nagoji is cropped at the chest and no hand is visible.

minors.description: The background Travancore guards look like East India Company sepoys rather than period Travancore troops. They wear red turbans with a front badge or plume, white jackets and drawers, crossed red belts and red cummerbunds. CONTINUITY says Travancore regulars wear a white mundu with crossed leather belts. They are not red coats, so the redcoat rule is not broken. Still, the red-turban, cross-belt sepoy look is late-18th and 19th-century British-Indian imagery. Similar crossed red belts and red sashes appear on the guards in 3.3 and 4.2.
minors.evidence: Page 6 bottom panel: the guards at left and centre between the pillars, behind Ibrahim and beside the brass lamp (zoom of about x=360-610, y=1630-1830).

minors.description: A background guard's headgear looks like a Santa hat at print size: a red cap with a fat white rolled band. At reading size it looks comic and anachronistic.
minors.evidence: Page 9, panel 2 (top right): the guard behind the spear between Varma and Ramayyan, just above the "He says I always see the two faces of the coin" balloon (about x=930, y=550).

minors.description: Behind the gate there is a whitewashed, two-storey European colonial house with a hipped tile roof and a belvedere tower. It reads as a Portuguese or Goan villa inside the Travancore fort. The script calls for a Kerala pillared hall and a laterite wall, so the building is out of place in the setting.
minors.evidence: Page 1, panel 4: the background between Nagoji's shoulder and Ibrahim's turban (about x=440-760, y=1290-1500).

minors.description: Two background figures on the quay are dressed in modern-looking clothes. One wears a short-sleeved white T-shirt-like top. The other wears a tucked tan short-sleeved shirt with a belt and loose trousers, which reads as 20th-century workwear rather than 1740s Malabar dress.
minors.evidence: Page 2, panel 4: small figures by the water, at upper left beside the pillar (about x=165, y=1260) and at right behind Ramayyan's table (about x=1000, y=1260).

minors.description: The hilltop fortress glimpsed through the pillars looks like a European medieval castle, with round crenellated towers on a hill. The same castle-on-a-hill backdrop recurs in 3.1, 3.3 and 4.2. The script describes a low laterite rampart running inland, so this reads as a stock European or Rajput castle rather than a Travancore fortification.
minors.evidence: Page 2, panel 5: the background to the left of Ibrahim (about x=310, y=1640). Also page 3 panel 1 (upper left, x=230, y=290), page 3 panel 3 (upper left, x=150, y=860) and page 4 panel 2 (upper right, x=1130, y=400).

minors.description: Ramayyan's palm leaf carries painted, blurry script-like marks around the stylus tip. These are pseudo-text in the art. They cannot be read and fit the writing action, but the no-text rule technically covers them. A clean leaf with stroke texture only would be safer.
minors.evidence: Page 4, top-left inset in panel 5: grey dash marks along the leaf to the right of the stylus point (about x=170-330, y=1590-1640).

minors.description: The chapter's lettering convention isn't followed. Each '[in Malayalam]' tag is set in upright dialogue type at normal size in a full-size balloon, but the script calls for a small balloon holding only an italic tag. The manner cues get no treatment either: VARMA (sharp) at 5.3 uses an ordinary balloon, and IBRAHIM (small, soft) at 1.3 and RAMAYYAN (soft) at 5.5 are set at normal size and weight.
minors.evidence: Zoomed crop of the 3.3 tag: '[in Malayalam]' is upright, the same face and size as Ramayyan's balloon beside it. Compare the 10.4 captions, which are clearly slanted italic. All nine tags in the chapter match the 3.3 one. The 1.3 'This is only one claw' balloon is the same size and weight as the 1.2 balloons.

minors.description: The tail on Ramayyan's off-panel line 'They questioned you.' ends at the top border directly above Varma's bangled wrist and extended fingers, so the line reads as Varma speaking Konkani. That breaks the chapter's rule that the king speaks only through the Malayalam tag.
minors.evidence: Crop of 3.5: the tail tip meets the top edge at about x=555 of the panel. Varma's arm enters from the top left, and his two fingers sit just below that point. No other figure's head is in frame.

minors.description: The panel widths are ragged. 3.1 is inset about 30px on each side, and 3.5 is a narrow centred panel inset about 300px on each side at 300 DPI, which leaves large cream margins on the bottom row. The approved Chapter 1 pages keep panels on one outer frame, with at most one slight inset.
minors.evidence: Panel scan, page 3: row 1 runs x=178 to 1659, rows 2 to 4 run 148 to 1689, and row 5 runs 444 to 1473 (frame is 148 to 1689).

minors.description: Ibrahim's second balloon ('He comes from Portuguese chains...') sits on Nagoji's bowing torso and over Varma's lap and the map. Its tail crosses Nagoji's back to reach Ibrahim's hand, so it nearly reads as Nagoji's line, and it hides the bow, which is the panel's action.
minors.evidence: Crop of 3.1: the tail runs from the balloon's left edge to Ibrahim's outstretched fingers, within about 30px of Nagoji's shoulder. The balloon body covers Nagoji's waist and the front of Varma's seat and map.

minors.description: The page layout is ragged. 4.3 and 4.4 are each centred at a different inset width. 4.4, which the script calls the page's biggest panel, comes out no larger than the full-width 4.5. The off-panel Nagoji balloon in 4.5 straddles the inset frame instead of sitting in it, and its tail runs the full height of the panel to end on the map beside Varma's pointing hand.
minors.evidence: Panel scan, page 4: 4.3 runs x=310 to 1528, 4.4 runs 370 to 1468, and 4.5 runs 148 to 1689. 4.4 and 4.5 are about 372k display px² each. In 4.5 the 'And their infantry...' balloon overlaps the inset border, and its tail ends at the bottom edge on the map.

minors.description: Balloon placement and gutter problems. In 5.2 both balloons press into the left, right and bottom panel borders and cover Nagoji's lap and hands, with tails aimed at his chest and shoulder. In 5.4 the 'I mistrust everyone...' balloon touches the left border. In the bottom row, 5.5 is inset about 22px at top and bottom relative to 5.4, so the row's top and bottom edges don't line up.
minors.evidence: Crops of 5.2 and the bottom row. Column scan: 5.4 runs y=1660 to 2542, while 5.5 runs about 1682 to 2520.

minors.description: The left panel border clips the bottom-left balloon ('That does not make my other calculations less true.'), and the line ends on the one-word widow 'true.'
minors.evidence: Crop: the balloon's left curve is cut off at the panel edge, and the second line holds only 'true.'

minors.description: Ramayyan's two balloons cover Varma's torso and nearly all of Ramayyan below the chin, so the translating figure is hidden. The right-hand balloon is a seven-line narrow column whose bottom touches the panel's bottom border.
minors.evidence: Crop of 7.3: the 'They have Dutch fortifications...' balloon runs from Ramayyan's chin to the bottom border. The left balloon spans Varma's chest to his waist.

minors.description: The art leaves almost no sky, so the two captions sit across the horizon line. They hide most of the 'hard, empty horizon' that the first caption ('Somewhere beyond that horizon...') points to. The script asked for open sky to hold the captions.
minors.evidence: Crop of 7.5: both caption boxes span the full height of the sky and overlap the sea line. Only a narrow gap of horizon shows between them, at about the centre of the panel.

minors.description: Crowded framing. In 8.1 and 8.4 the top border crops Nagoji's head, and the balloons flank or cover his body. In 8.1 the 'You have guns and forts...' balloon covers his knees and bandaged hands. In 8.4 the script asked for open hall space above him for the balloons. In 8.2 the first balloon covers the legs and splash of the lead horses in the middle of the charge.
minors.evidence: Crops: in 8.1 Nagoji's hair touches the top edge, and the right balloon covers his lap. In 8.4 his hair is cut by the top border, and the right balloon's top meets the border. In 8.2 the 'What you do not yet have...' balloon spans the horses' lower bodies.

minors.description: The first balloon ('The Madurai horsemen know the straight charge...') is a tall eight-line column that touches the top border and is clipped by the left one. The second balloon also butts against the top border.
minors.evidence: Crop of 9.1: the balloon's left curve is cut at x≈0 of the panel, with short line breaks such as 'the straight / charge. They do'.

minors.description: Balloon clipping and tail placement. In 10.2 the top border clips the '[in Malayalam]' balloon, and its tail aims at the peacock feather on the turban instead of Varma's mouth. Ramayyan's second balloon is a tall column ending on the widow 'it.' and covers both men's laps. In 10.3 the left panel border clips the 'Come. Let us see...' balloon.
minors.evidence: Crop of 10.2: the tag balloon's top is flush with the border, and its tail tip sits beside the feather at the top right of the turban. In 10.3 the balloon's left side is cut at the panel edge.

minors.description: The script asks for the chapter's closing caption to be set separate and weighted. Here it is an ordinary caption box, placed in Nagoji's line of sight up the coast, so it covers the coastline he is looking toward. The top border also crops his head.
minors.evidence: Crop of 10.5: the 'For now, Travancore was the forge...' box is the same style as every other caption. It sits immediately right of Nagoji's profile over the far coast, and his hair is cut by the top edge.

minors.description: Nagoji looks seated or crouched, forearms resting on his knees, while Ibrahim whispers. In the script he has just walked in: he walks into the clear space at 2.5 and only sits when told to at 4.2.
minors.evidence: At the bottom edge, below the 'Remember what I said about gifts' balloon, Nagoji's bandaged forearms lie crossed over bent knees in a seated pose.

minors.description: The tail of Ibrahim's balloon 'Marthanda Varma. And his diwan.' ends on the back of Nagoji's head rather than at Ibrahim's mouth, which makes the speaker ambiguous.
minors.evidence: The tail tip lands on Nagoji's hair behind his ear, roughly 70 px left of Ibrahim's nose (around x=1300, y=1290 in the original).

minors.description: The script marks 2.2, the silent first reveal of the king, as 'Large'. It is drawn as a half-width panel the same size as 2.3 and much smaller than the 2.1 establishing shot, which weakens the reveal.
minors.evidence: Row 2 is split into two equal panels (2.2 left, 2.3 right). 2.1 above is full width and taller.

minors.description: Framing differs from the script. 3.1 should be shot from the entrance end, with the open side on screen left and Varma small at the far end beside Ramayyan at his low table. The render is a lateral medium shot: Varma sits mid-frame at close range, Ramayyan stands writing at the far right with no table, and the open side shows a hill fort rather than the sea.
minors.evidence: Varma's head and shoulders are at about the same scale as Nagoji's. Ramayyan stands upright holding a palm-leaf bundle. The opening at the top left shows a hilltop fortress.

minors.description: In this fast question-and-answer panel, Nagoji should answer the platform. He looks up and away to screen right, toward the edge of the panel. His bandaged hands are hidden behind the two 'I did.' balloons.
minors.evidence: At the far right, Nagoji's head is turned up to the right, away from Ramayyan and Varma at the left. Both 'I did.' balloons cover his torso and hands.

minors.description: Missing gesture: in the script Nagoji's bandaged hand shapes a low wall in the air as he describes the bastions. The render is a head-and-shoulders crop with no hand.
minors.evidence: Only Nagoji's head and upper chest show at the lower centre. The bastion stain is at the left and the balloon at the right.

minors.description: The script makes 1.3 the largest panel on the page. It shares row 2 at half width, and 1.4 is larger. Ibrahim's line is marked (small, soft) but is set in a full-size standard balloon.
minors.evidence: 1.3 is about 550x615 px in the displayed page; 1.4 is full width at about 1110x415. The 'This is only one claw...' balloon is the same size as the balloons in 1.2.

minors.description: The guards don't match the script. They should wear white cotton with dark sashes and carry matchlocks. They are bare-chested with leather cross-belts and carry only spears. A whitewashed, European-style two-storey building with arched windows and a red tile roof stands behind the gate, which the script doesn't call for and which suggests a European presence inside Varma's fort. A similar building sits on the wall in 7.3.
minors.evidence: Behind Nagoji and Ibrahim, a white mansion with arched windows rises above the red wall. The three guards wear brown leather straps over bare torsos, and no matchlock is visible.

minors.description: The script calls 6.1 a wide shot from the entrance end, with the hall gone still and the sea through the open side. It is drawn as a quarter-page panel, and no sea shows through the open side.
minors.evidence: 6.1 fills only the top-left quadrant. Its left edge shows pillars and a palm but no water.

minors.description: In the script this point-of-view shot looks down from the hall to the inlet and a hard, empty horizon, with open sky kept for the captions. The panel is a short strip at ground level looking straight onto a beach, and the two captions cover most of the sky and much of the horizon line.
minors.evidence: The captions span almost the full width at the top. The horizon shows only in a narrow gap between them, with a boat mast standing on it. The beach is at eye level, not below.

minors.description: The present-day Nagoji should be small at the bottom edge so the memory dominates. He is drawn at mid size in the lower left. The first balloon sits over the point of impact where the horses meet the Portuguese line, which hides the 'felt it break' moment.
minors.evidence: Seated Nagoji is about a third of the panel's height. 'What you do not yet have...' covers the centre, where the lead cavalry reaches the musketeers.
